QF.id: Income, Residential Status, Five Heads of Income_3

question.text: Mr. Suresh, a Person of Indian Origin (PIO) settled in Canada, visited India for 130 days during PY 2024-25. His stay in India during the 4 preceding years totalled 380 days. His Indian income for the year is Rs.10 lakh. What is his residential status?

explanation.text: The Logic: For a PIO who is visiting India and whose Indian income is Rs.15 lakh or less, the workbook requires 182 days in India in the current previous year. Mr. Suresh was present for only 130 days, which is less than 182, so he fails the basic condition and is a Non-Resident. The relaxed 120-day threshold for PIOs applies only when Indian income exceeds Rs.15 lakh, which is not the case here. The Trap: Candidates may apply the 60-day or 120-day rule without first checking the income threshold and the "visiting India" status. For a visiting PIO with Indian income up to Rs.15 lakh, the 182-day requirement controls. Note: The 60-day basic-condition leg can still apply to PIOs who are not visiting India; it is the visiting-PIO scenario that triggers the 182-day rule when income is up to Rs.15 lakh.
